review: 1:1–1:3 — the Arabic's three questions (were You slain, did You taste, did You bow) are Isaiah 53 in question form; Hebrew keeps the interrogative הֲ only on the first verb, which carries the whole stanza.

2:2 נִדְכָּא נִדְכָּא — the doubling of the Arabic سُحِقْتَ سَحْقًا ('crushed with crushing') is a cognate accusative; Hebrew repeats the participle instead, since a noun of the same root would add a syllable.
2:4 בַּעֲוֺן פִּשְׁעִי הָרָע — 'for the guilt of my evil transgression'; the Arabic ذَنْبِيَ الْمَعِيب ('my faulty guilt') is one noun phrase, and Hebrew needs the construct to reach eight syllables.
3:4 עָלַי הָעֱנִי הַזֶּה — the Arabic repeats عَنِّي أَنَا ('for me') four times in stanza 3; Hebrew carries the emphasis with the fronted עָלַי and the demonstrative, so the question lands.
4:1 עָלַי כֵּן עָלַי — word-for-word the Arabic عَنِّي أَنَا نَعَمْ عَنِّي; the answer to stanza 3 must sound like the same voice.
